data.title: Klátova Nová Ves – Šiance, one of the largest hillforts in Slovakia
data.excerpt: Deep in the woods of the Tríbeč, 9.35 ha are enclosed by ramparts so massive that Šiance ranks among the largest hillforts in Slovakia. The Lusatian culture built it at the end of the Bronze Age; the Slavs rebuilt it in the 8th – 10th centuries and left behind a rich hoard of metal objects, among them smith's tools and pieces linked to the Avar milieu, although they probably used the site only as a refuge.
data.metaTitle: Klátova Nová Ves – Šiance, a vast hillfort in the Tríbeč
data.metaDescription: Šiance in the Tríbeč covers 9.35 ha and its exceptionally massive ramparts rank it among the largest hillforts in Slovakia; built by the Lusatian culture.

keyFacts.label: Location
keyFacts.value: The Tríbeč mountains, south of Klátova Nová Ves, 460.0 m above sea level

keyFacts.label: Defences
keyFacts.value: An exceptionally massive rampart system, one of the largest in Slovakia

keyFacts.label: Cultures that occupied the site
keyFacts.value: The Lusatian culture (the Bronze Age, the Hallstatt period), the Slavs (8th – 10th century)

keyFacts.label: Entrance to the hillfort
keyFacts.value: At least two gateways, the most massive defences by the south-western gateway

keyFacts.label: Notable finds
keyFacts.value: Smith's tools, arrowheads, armament and horse harness with Avar elements

timeline.description: At the end of the Hallstatt period the Lusatian culture disappeared and many of its fortifications were taken over by the people of the Púchov culture, but we know of no finds of the La Tène and Roman periods from the hillfort of Šiance, so it was evidently not in use then.

timeline.description: Two hoards were found at the hillfort – smith's tools (two hammers and an anvil) and eight arrowheads with sockets and barbs; further finds include armament, dress and parts of horse harness with elements linked to the Avar milieu.

timeline.title: The hillfort as a temporary refuge
timeline.description: In spite of the rich hoards, the faint traces of occupation inside the hillfort testify that it was not permanently inhabited – archaeologists assume that the Slavs used it only temporarily as a refuge in times of danger.

children.text: The hillfort of Šiance is located in the Tríbeč mountains, on an upland site called Šiance (460.0 m), south of the village of Klátova Nová Ves. It was built above a stream in the northern belt of the Tríbeč, about 1 kilometre as the crow flies from Javorový vrch. It is a very extensive hillfort with an area of 9.35 ha and with exceptionally massive rampart defences, which undoubtedly rank among the largest in Slovakia.

The hillfort was built by the people of the Lusatian culture at the end of the Bronze Age and was used by them during the Early Iron Age (the Hallstatt period). The dense occupation of the hillfort in this period is proved by the large quantity of pottery fragments typical of the Lusatian culture. Sometime at the end of the Hallstatt period the Lusatian culture disappears, and many of its fortifications were later used by the people of the Púchov culture in the La Tène and Roman periods. From this period, however, we so far know of no finds from the hillfort, so it was evidently not in use then.

children.text: Its renewed reconstruction and use are the work of our ancestors the Slavs in the 8th – 10th centuries, who left behind here, besides sherd material, also a rich hoard of metal objects containing – apart from agricultural implements, a battle axe (a bearded axe) and other items – for instance a rattle that still works. Among the remarkable finds are parts of armament and of dress, or of horse harness. Many of them are linked to the Avar milieu (an openwork spearhead, a stirrup, a mount in the shape of a boar's head, belt mounts), so this could be a matter of close trade contacts with the area of the Avar Khaganate or of war booty; but it may equally be a source of raw material for a craftsman, who could in this way have used Avar objects that were already „unfashionable“ in the later – Great Moravian – period for further working. Further finds (small hammers, an anvil) prove the presence of craftsmen at the hillfort; a spur, a bearded axe or a stirrup, on the other hand, suggest the presence of warriors. Two hoards were also found: the first contained the smith's tools already mentioned – two hammers and an anvil; in the second there were eight arrowheads with sockets and barbs, which were in use in the Slavic period. On the basis of the faint traces of occupation inside the hillfort, however, archaeologists assume that, in spite of the rich hoards, the hillfort was not permanently inhabited in the 8th to 10th centuries, and that the Slavs therefore used it only temporarily as a refuge, that is as a place where they hid and defended themselves against the enemy in times of danger.

The hillfort was entered through at least two gateways, and settlement pits, hearths and further finds were discovered on its interior area. In the area of the presumed south-western gateway the defences are especially massive, and in its vicinity there is an information panel with basic information about the hillfort. I can only praise this, even though the absence of any signposts (plus the fact that the tourist route, or educational trail, is not marked in the terrain) makes it quite difficult for walkers to find the hillfort, which is fairly well hidden deep in the woods of the Tríbeč. But at least this is a good place to get lost; after all… you are in the Tríbeč…
